chunks: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
Water purifies and is not (itself) purified.

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: Water — in jurisprudence, specifically refers to pure (tahir) water capable of purifying (mutahhir)
key_terms.يُطَهَّرُ: Is purified (passive voice, Form II) — the water is not acted upon; it does not need purification from an external agent
key_terms.يُطَهِّرُ: Purifies (active voice, Form II) — the water acts as the purifying agent

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling that water purifies and is not itself purified?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the foundational principle of Islamic ritual purity law (tahara) concerning water: pure water has the intrinsic capacity to purify other things, yet it does not require purification itself. This ruling, narrated through a chain reaching Imam al-Sadiq (AS) back to the Prophet (SAWW), underpins the entire jurisprudential framework for ritual purity in Shia fiqh, particularly governing which water may be used for wudu, ghusl, and the purification of najis objects.
